academic_translation:
If my suffering
Does not harm the bodies of others,
Even so, that suffering is mine,
Unbearable due to clinging to self.

locked_terms.use: holding on tightly to a self

translation: My suffering does not hurt the bodies of others. Even so, that suffering is mine. It is unbearable because of holding on tightly to a self.

academic_translation:
Likewise, although the sufferings of others
Do not fall upon me,
Even so, that suffering is mine,
Difficult to bear due to clinging to self.

locked_terms.use: holding on tightly to a self

translation: In the same way, the suffering of others does not fall on me. Even so, that suffering is mine. It is hard to bear because of holding on tightly to a self.

academic_translation:
I should dispel the suffering of others
Because it is suffering, like my own suffering.
I should benefit others
Because they are sentient beings, like my own body.
translation: I should take away the suffering of others. It is suffering, just like my own suffering. I should help other living beings. They are like my very own body.

academic_translation:
When both myself and others
Are equal in desiring happiness,
What difference is there with myself,
That I strive for my own happiness alone?
translation: Other people want happiness just as much as I do. We are exactly the same. So why do I only work for my own happiness?

academic_translation:
When both myself and others
Are equal in not desiring suffering,
What difference is there with myself,
That I protect myself and not others?
translation: Other people hate suffering just as much as I do. We are exactly the same. So why do I protect myself and not others?

academic_translation:
If, because their suffering
Does not harm me, I do not protect them,
If future suffering also
Does not harm me, why protect against it?
translation: If I do not protect others because their suffering does not hurt me, why do I protect myself from future suffering? That future suffering does not hurt me right now.

academic_translation:
Thinking "I will experience it"—
That conceptual thought is false;
For the one who dies is indeed another,
And the one who is born is also another.
translation: Thinking that I will experience it is false. The person who dies is someone else, and the person who is born is also someone else.

academic_translation:
If whenever anyone's suffering
Must be protected by that person alone,
The suffering of the foot is not the hand's;
Why should it be protected by it?
translation: If everyone only has to protect themselves from their own suffering, think about the foot. The suffering of the foot is not the hand's suffering. So why does the hand protect the foot?

academic_translation:
If you say, "Even if it is illogical, here
One engages through grasping at a self,"
Whatever is illogical regarding self and other
Is precisely what should be abandoned to the best of one's ability.
translation: You might say, "Even if it makes no sense, we act by holding on to a self." But anything that makes no sense about yourself and others should be given up as best as you can.

academic_translation:
What are called a continuum and a collection
Are false, like a garland, an army, and so forth;
Since there is no one who possesses suffering,
Therefore, who will have control over this?
translation: A continuing stream and a collection of parts are not real things. They are just words, like a necklace or an army. Since no one truly owns suffering, who is there to control it?

academic_translation:
Since suffering has no owner,
All are entirely without distinction;
Because it is suffering, it is to be dispelled—
What is the point of making restrictions there?
translation: Suffering has no owner. Because of this, everyone is exactly the same. Because it is suffering, it must be cleared away. What is the point of making rules about who to help?
Someone might ask, "Why should we stop the suffering of everyone?" There is no room to argue. If we stop it, we must stop all of it. If not, then I must suffer just like any other living being.

academic_translation:
If you ask, "Since compassion results in much suffering,
Why forcibly generate it?"
When one contemplates the suffering of wandering beings,
How is the suffering of compassion great?
translation: Someone might ask, "Since compassion brings so much suffering, why force yourself to feel it?" But think about the suffering of all beings. Compared to that, how is the suffering of compassion great?

academic_translation:
If by means of a single suffering
Many sufferings are eliminated,
By the compassionate one, that suffering
Should certainly be generated for oneself and others.
translation: If facing one single suffering removes many other sufferings, a kind person should gladly accept it. They should be willing to bring about that suffering for themselves and others.

academic_translation:
Therefore, Supuṣpacandra,
Even knowing the harm from the king,
Did not dispel his own suffering,
So that the suffering of many would be exhausted.
translation: This is why Supushpachandra did not stop his own suffering. He knew the king would hurt him. He did this so the suffering of many would end.

academic_translation:
Thus, one whose continuum is habituated,
Because of delighting in pacifying others' suffering,
Like a swan into a lotus pool,
Will plunge even into the Avīci hell.
translation: When my continuing stream gets used to this, I will love calming the suffering of others. I will dive right into the Avichi hell to help them. I will dive in like a swan landing in a lotus pond.

academic_translation:
When sentient beings are liberated,
The ocean of joy that exists—
Is that itself not sufficient?
What is the use of desiring liberation?
translation: When living beings are freed, there is an ocean of joy. Is that joy not enough? What is the use of wanting freedom just for myself?

academic_translation:
Therefore, even when acting for the welfare of others,
There is no conceit or amazement.
Because of delighting solely in the welfare of others,
There is no hope for a ripened result.
translation: So even when I work for the good of others, I am not proud or amazed. I only find joy in the good of others. I do not hope for a result that ripens for me.

academic_translation:
Therefore, just as I protect myself
From even the slightest unpleasant word,
Likewise, a protective mind toward others
And a mind of compassion should be cultivated in this way.
translation: I protect myself from even the smallest mean word. I should protect others in the exact same way. I must grow a mind of compassion like this.

academic_translation:
Through habituation, regarding others'
Drops of semen and blood,
Even though there is an absence of an entity,
Just as one knows them as "I",
translation: I grew used to thinking of drops from others as my own body. Even though they are without a thing that is really me, I call them 'I'.

academic_translation:
Likewise, regarding the bodies of others too,
Why are they not apprehended as "I"?
Positing my own body as other
Is in that way not difficult.
translation: In the same way, why don't I see other people's bodies as "me"? Thinking of my own body as "other" is not hard to do.

academic_translation:
Having known that oneself has faults, and that others too
Are oceans of good qualities,
One should meditate on completely discarding self-grasping
And taking up others.
translation: I should know that I have faults and that others are oceans of good qualities. I must meditate on completely letting go of holding on to a self, and taking up others instead.

academic_translation:
Just as hands and so forth
Are accepted as limbs of the body,
Likewise, as limbs of wandering beings,
Why are embodied beings not accepted?
translation: We accept that hands and other parts belong to the body. In the same way, why don't we accept that beings with a body are parts of all beings?

academic_translation: Just as towards this body of selflessness, The intellect of self has arisen through habituation, Likewise towards other sentient beings as well, Why should the intellect of self not arise through habituation?
translation: By getting used to it, the thinking mind of self has grown toward this body with no separate self. In the same way, why shouldn't the thinking mind of self grow toward other living beings by getting used to it?

academic_translation:
If it is like that, even having accomplished
The welfare of others, amazement and conceit do not arise,
Just as when one has eaten food oneself,
Hope for a return does not arise.
translation: If it is like that, doing the good of others will not make me feel amazed or proud. This is just like eating food myself. I do not hope for a reward when I eat.

academic_translation:
Therefore, just as I protect myself
From even minor unpleasantness,
Likewise, a protective mind toward wandering beings
And a mind of compassion should be habituated.
translation: Therefore, just as I protect myself from even tiny unpleasant things, I should get used to having a protective mind and a mind of compassion toward all beings.

academic_translation:
Therefore, the Protector Avalokiteśvara,
Out of great compassion,
In order to dispel even wandering beings' fear in assemblies,
Bestowed a blessing upon even his own name.
translation: The Protector Avalokiteshvara felt great compassion. He wanted to take away the fear that beings feel in crowds. So, he put a blessing on his own name.

academic_translation:
One should not turn back from hardship;
For through the power of habituation in this way,
Even someone whose name caused fear to hear,
Without them, one becomes joyless.
translation: I should not give up when things are hard. The power of getting used to things changes us. You might once be scared to even hear someone's name. But later, you might feel no joy without them.

academic_translation:
Whoever wishes to quickly protect
Themselves and others,
Should practice the exchange of self and others,
The supreme secret.
translation: Do you want to quickly protect yourself and others? Then you should practice the exchange of self and others. This is the greatest secret.

academic_translation:
Through attachment to this body of mine,
Fear arises toward small sources of fear;
That body which gives rise to fear,
Who would not hate as an enemy?
translation: Through clinging to this body of mine, I feel afraid of even small things. Since this body creates so much fear, who would not hate it like an enemy?

academic_translation:
Whoever, wishing to perform the treatment to cure
The body's illnesses of hunger, thirst, and the like,
Kills birds, fish, and wild animals,
And lies in ambush along the roads;
translation: People want to cure their body's hunger and thirst. To do this, they kill birds, fish, and wild animals. They even wait in hiding along the roads.

academic_translation:
If one, for the sake of profit and respect,
Kills even their father and mother,
And, having stolen the wealth of the Three Jewels,
Is thereby burned in the Avīci hell,
translation: Some want money and respect so much that they even kill their own parents. They steal wealth from the Three Jewels. Because of this, they will burn in the Avichi hell.

academic_translation:
What wise person would desire,
Protect, and venerate that body?
Who would not view this
As an enemy, and despise it?
translation: What wise person would want, protect, and honor that body? Who would not see it as an enemy and dislike it?

academic_translation:
"If I give, what will I consume?"
Thinking of one's own welfare is the way of a demon.
"If I consume, what will I give?"
Thinking of the welfare of others is the way of a god.
translation: "If I give this away, what will I use?" Thinking of my own good is the way of a demon. "If I use this, what will I give away?" Thinking of the good of others is the way of a god.

academic_translation:
If one harms others for one's own sake,
One will be tormented in hell and so forth.
If one harms oneself for the sake of others,
One will obtain all excellence.
translation: If I harm others for my own sake, I will suffer in hell. If I harm myself for the sake of others, I will gain all excellence.

academic_translation:
Through wishing for oneself to be exalted,
One will be reborn in a lower realm, base, and stupid.
If that very wish is shifted to others,
One will obtain a happy realm and respect.
translation: If I only wish to be great, I will be reborn in an unhappy realm as someone low and foolish. If I shift that wish to others, I will gain a happy realm and respect.

academic_translation:
If one employs others for one's own welfare,
One will experience servitude and the like.
If one employs oneself for the welfare of others,
One will experience lordship and the like.
translation: If I use others for my own good, I will become a servant. If I use myself for the good of others, I will become a master.

academic_translation:
Whatever happiness there is in the world,
It all arises from wishing for the happiness of others.
Whatever suffering there is in the world,
It all arises from wishing for one's own happiness.
translation: Whatever happiness there is in the world comes from wishing for the happiness of others. Whatever suffering there is in the world comes from wishing for my own happiness.

academic_translation:
What need is there to say much?
The childish one who acts for their own welfare, and
The Sage who acts for the welfare of others—
Look at the difference between these two!
translation: Why say more? A childish person acts only for their own good. The Sage acts for the good of others. Just look at the difference between them!

academic_translation:
If one does not truly exchange
One's own happiness and the suffering of others,
Buddhahood will not be achieved,
And even in saṃsāra there is no happiness.
translation: If I do not exchange my own happiness for the suffering of others, I will never reach the state of a Buddha. Even in the cycle of rebirth, I will find no happiness.
